text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.83% today, continuing a steep two-week slide of 8.36% that began right after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The immediate pressure came from oil prices—US crude dropped to $99.64 per barrel, and more significantly, Brent crude briefly broke below $90 for the first time since August after Trump said he expects the Iran conflict to end "fairly soon." Lower crude prices directly cut into the revenue and profits of oil producers like ConocoPhillips, and the market is pricing in the possibility of further weakness if geopolitical tensions ease.

The timing matters: the stock has been falling steadily since earnings landed, suggesting the quarterly results themselves disappointed investors or reset expectations downward, and the Iran news on Monday simply accelerated what was already a negative trend. Weaker crude prices hit oil majors harder than most stocks because their core business depends on sustained high energy costs.
